title: Where exactly
description: Say exactly where something is, and where it is going.
grammar: prepositions of place, and the words of direction
grammarNote: Near and far take de: cerca de la estación, lejos del centro.

explanation.summary: Prepositions of place in Spanish are more exact than English ones. English often leaves the preposition out, Spanish nearly always needs it. A unit of distance becomes a phrase with de attached to it.

sections.heading: Near and far take de
sections.body: In English you say near the station. In Spanish it is cerca de la estación. The same is true of lejos: lejos del centro. The de is not optional, and it attaches to the phrase that follows it.

examples.es: El hotel está cerca de la estación.
examples.en: The hotel is near the station.

examples.es: Mi casa está lejos del centro.
examples.en: My house is far from the centre.

examples.es: El banco está frente al edificio.
examples.en: The bench is opposite the building.

sections.heading: Position words
sections.body: Entre is between, detrás is behind, delante is in front of, encima is on top of, debajo is underneath. Inside and outside take de as well: dentro de la caja, fuera de la ciudad. And hacia points in a direction without arriving: hacia el norte.

examples.es: La tienda está entre el banco y la fuente.
examples.en: The shop is between the bench and the fountain.

examples.es: El gato está detrás de la puerta.
examples.en: The cat is behind the door.
We are heading towards the bridge.

sections.heading: Where it is, where it went
sections.body: Estar says where a thing is now: la caja está encima de la mesa. Ir says where it is going: la caja va encima de la mesa. The preposition does not change; the verb does.

examples.es: El libro está debajo del sofá.
examples.en: The book is underneath the sofa.

examples.es: Pongo el libro encima de la mesa.
examples.en: I put the book on the table.

items.note: Entre la cocina y el salón.
Encima de la mesa. It also means above.
Hacia el norte. It points in a direction without arriving.
Masculine: el frente. As a preposition: frente a.
Feminine: la esquina. You already know this one from the neighbourhood unit.

drills.prompt: El hotel está cerca ___ la estación.
drills.meaning: the hotel is near the station

drills.prompt: La tienda está ___ el banco y la fuente.
drills.meaning: the shop is between the bench and the fountain
the cat is behind the door
we are heading towards the bridge
the book is underneath the sofa
